newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MAN UTD STAY TOP, MORE WOE FOR MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MAN UTD STAY TOP, MORE WOE FOR MILAN.

text.p: A brilliant volleyed goal by midfielder David Beckham earned English league leaders Manchester United a point from a 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge on Saturday after Gianfranco Zola had put Chelsea ahead.
Second placed Liverpool managed only a 0-0 draw at home to Blackburn while Newcastle moved into third after beating Middlesbrough 1-0.
Arsenal's title challenge was effectively ended with a 1-0 home defeat by Wimbledon on Sunday.
ITALY
Milan's nightmare season continued when they lost 1-0 to lowly Perugia, had Paolo Maldini and Christophe Dugarry both sent off for elbowing and lost Edgar Davids with a broken leg.
The defeat leaves Milan in 11th place.
League leaders Juventus, who had their bus stoned before their match in Florence, drew 1-1 away to 10-man Fiorentina but stayed five points clear of Sampdoria who recorded the same result at Napoli.
SPAIN
Barcelona striker Ronaldo and Real Madrid's Davor Suker each scored hat-tricks in big wins for the top two.
Real stayed six points ahead of their arch-rivals after hammering Oviedo 6-1 while Barcelona thrashed Zaragoza 4-1.
Third placed Betis lost ground after going down 3-0 to Deportivo Coruna.
GERMANY

Bayern Munich extended their Bundesliga lead to three points with a 1-1 draw at Bochum - Juergen Klinsmann the man on target for Bayern. Second-placed Borussia Dortmund lost 2-0 at Fortuna Duessldorf on Friday.
HOLLAND
Feyenoord missed the chance of going level with PSV at the top of the Dutch league when they were beaten 3-0 at arch-rivals Ajax Amsterdam.
It left PSV, 2-1 home winners over AZ Alkmaar on Saturday, three points ahead of Feyenoord with Twente Enschede third on 46.
FRANCE
Monaco slumped to their first French league defeat for more than three months when they lost 2-0 to Metz.
The defeat cut their lead over second-placed PSG to six points after the Parisians drew 1-1 at home to Guingamp.
Third-placed Bastia, who have a game in hand, are just a point behind PSG after beating lowly Nancy 2-0.
PORTUGAL
Portuguese champions Porto suffered their first defeat of the season when they were beaten 2-1 at home by Salgueiros on Sunday - but they till have a 13-point lead at the top.
